_comment: Enemy sensor positions are ALWAYS operator input. Nothing in this codebase detects, identifies or locates anything - it computes geometry from coordinates a human entered. Positions must fall inside the loaded map: lat 48.0001 to 48.3399, lon 24.2304 to 24.7693.
_placementNote: Threats sit 1.5-2.0 km from the corridor on ground that ACTUALLY OVERWATCHES it - each was chosen by computing how much of the route it can see at 15 m AGL, not by picking the highest peak. Corrected 2026-08-15 (third revision). Revision one used distant summits that only threatened the route because ranges were an invented 20-30 km. Revision two fixed the ranges but kept them 2.4 km out, where terrain blocked them and the route saw 2-6 seconds of exposure - honest and useless. A sensor covering a valley sits on the shoulder above it.

threats.label: east ridge observation post
threats.rangeSource: NATO STO MSG-SET-183 (as of 2025-11, sto.nato.int): purpose-built optical systems detect DJI-class drones in excess of 1.5 km in daylight, classification ~1 km with a 30x PTZ camera. An unaided observer performs worse. 2 km is generous for a human with optics.

threats.label: west ridge EW mast
threats.rangeSource: United24 (as of 2026-02, united24media.com): fielded Ukrainian RF drone-detection system with a ~4 km detection range.

threats.label: south approach radar
threats.rangeSource: Australian Army Occasional Paper 29 (as of 2024-10, researchcentre.army.gov.au): Mavic-class quadcopters are detected by target-detection radar at only 3-4 km.

_missionNote: 12 km along a valley rather than across the ridges, and 229 m of straight-line climb. Chosen so the endurance check passes for a quadcopter: a 58 km diagonal across the whole box was geometrically fine and unflyable by every platform.
_startNote: Start sits on 5 degree ground. An earlier version was 90 m away on a 30.3 degree slope, which the tracked UGV could not leave - and the old candidate-sampling router returned a 16.5 km route from it anyway, crossing 11 impassable cells and reporting the endurance as OK.
_vehicleNote: mission.vehicle takes a class ("ground", "air", "all") or a specific platform id ("ugvTracked", "quadLow", ...). A class plans for every platform in it so the trade-off stays visible. Ground vehicles go around obstacles of any height; aircraft are stopped only by obstacles that reach their operating altitude.
_rangeNote: SENSOR RANGES ARE SOURCED, NOT INVENTED (corrected 2026-08-15). An earlier version used 20-30 km, which is roughly ten times what open sources support against a small drone. Every value below now carries its source in rangeSource. Important caveat: there is NO published dataset for UNAIDED human detection ranges in this terrain - 'a soldier detects a tank at X km' is not documented in accessible sources. All figures below are SENSOR performance benchmarks used as proxies, and should be cited as such rather than as what a person can see. Full dossier: Research/Web/2026-08-15 - realistic visual detection range line of sight for a soldier observer spotting d.md
